newsitem.title: FINLAND: Housing costs drove Finnish April CPI rise up.
newsitem.headline: Housing costs drove Finnish April CPI rise up.

text.p: The rise in Finnish consumer prices accelerated to 1.0 percent year-on-year in April, boosted by a 0.5 percent month-on-month climb due mainly to more expensive housing, Statistics Finland (SF) said on Thursday.
"Almost half the rise was due to more expensive apartments," SF said in a statement. It was referring to the CPI rise in April over March of half a percentage point.
Electricity prices, more expensive vegetables and higher air travel costs also pulled the index higher, SF said.
Finland's consumer price index harmonised with EU-standards rose slightly less than the national index.
"Housing costs are not included in the harmonised basket," an SF official said by telephone.
The EU-harmonised CPI rose 0.3 percent in April on March for a year-on-year rise of 0.9 percent.
